title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinion on Dynamic Adjustment of Judge Quotas in People's Courts Below the Provincial Level (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Dynamic Adjustment of Judge Quotas in People's Courts Below the Provincial Level (for Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2020] No. 3

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions on Dynamic Adjustment of Judge Quotas in People's Courts Below the Provincial Level (for Trial Implementation) have been reviewed and adopted at the meeting of the Leading Party Group of the Supreme People's Court and are hereby issued to you. Please promptly forward them to the intermediate and basic people's courts within your jurisdiction, organize serious study, and implement them earnestly in light of actual conditions. Any circumstances or issues encountered during the work shall be promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

January 8, 2020

Guiding Opinions on Dynamic Adjustment of Judge Quotas in People's Courts Below the Provincial Level (for Trial Implementation)

For the purpose of achieving refined management of judge quotas, establishing a scientific, efficient, and trial work-oriented mechanism for the allocation, adjustment, and management of judge quotas, and in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts, the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant provisions, and in line with the spirit of the Central Government's promotion of judicial system reform, and in light of the actual work of the people's courts, these Opinions are formulated.

1. The overall allocation of judge quotas shall take provinces (autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government) as the unit, and shall not exceed the proportional range set by the Central Government.

2. Judge quotas of people's courts below the provincial level shall be subject to overall management by the High People's Court within the approved total amount. In principle, with cities divided into districts (prefectures) as units, they shall be reasonably allocated and dynamically adjusted within the provincial scope. The High People's Court of a municipality directly under the Central Government may incorporate the judge quotas of intermediate and basic people's courts within its jurisdiction into overall management.

An intermediate people's court established within a province or autonomous region may carry out overall allocation and dynamic adjustment of judge quotas within its jurisdiction.

3. The allocation of judge quotas in basic people's courts shall be based primarily on the approved staffing, total number of cases handled, and average number of cases handled per judge.

The allocation of quotas in high and intermediate people's courts may, on the basis of the approved staffing, total number of cases handled, and average number of cases handled per judge, appropriately take into account the workload of business guidance to lower-level courts and other work.

4. Allocation of judge quotas shall be skewed toward basic-level courts and the front line of case handling. The proportion of judge quotas in a High People's Court shall not be higher than the average level of basic people's courts within its jurisdiction.

5. A higher people's court may, based on changes in the workload of judges handling cases in courts within its jurisdiction, as well as the personnel staffing, institutional setup, number of cases, number of judges, and other circumstances, decide to adjust the allocation of judge quotas.

6. A higher people's court may reserve a reasonable proportion or number of judge quotas for adjustment and allocation within its jurisdiction. The judge quotas reserved by a higher people's court for dynamic adjustment shall, in principle, not be used for the court itself.

7. Where a higher people's court adjusts and allocates judge quotas among courts within its jurisdiction, it may adjust and use the reserved judge quotas, or it may carry out overall adjustment of judge quotas already allocated to various courts.

8. Where any of the following circumstances occurs, the judge quotas shall be adjusted in a timely manner:

(1) The number of cases in a court increases substantially, and the judge quota is obviously unable to meet the needs of case handling work;

(2) Due to adjustment of administrative divisions, abolition or establishment of institutions, or other reasons, the court's staffing undergoes a significant adjustment, and the number of cases or workload undergoes a major change;

(3) The number of cases handled by judges is relatively small, and there is obvious idleness;

(4) Other circumstances where it is truly necessary to adjust the quotas.

9. The High People's Court shall regularly conduct comprehensive investigation and assessment of the personnel staffing, number of cases, quota proportion, and average case handling workload per judge of courts within its jurisdiction, and put forward opinions on dynamic adjustment and use, which shall be implemented after review and decision by the Leading Party Group of the court.

10. Where a higher people's court carries out a comprehensive adjustment of judge quotas of courts within its jurisdiction, in principle, it shall not exceed twice during the term of office of one president, and frequent adjustments shall be avoided.

11. Real-time dynamic adjustment of judge quotas shall, in principle, be proposed by the people's court with adjustment needs and submitted to the higher people's court for approval. Where an intermediate people's court adjusts the allocation of judge quotas of people's courts within its jurisdiction, it shall report to the High People's Court for record.

12. The High People's Court shall, based on the usage of judge quotas in courts within its jurisdiction, promptly coordinate the adjustment of judge quotas and initiate the work of appointing judges to the quota, supplementation, and withdrawal.

13. The High People's Court shall establish a normalized supplementation mechanism for quota judges, and regularly conduct selection for quotas reserved or vacated in courts within its jurisdiction. In principle, selection of quota judges shall be conducted no less than once per year.

14. In the selection of quota judges, when recommending candidates to be appointed to the quota to the provincial judges selection committee, factors such as the average case handling workload per quota judge of the court and the number of judges expected to retire shortly may be comprehensively considered, and alternate candidates shall be recommended at a proportion not exceeding 30% of the number of vacant judge quotas. Before the next selection of judges is initiated, a court with vacancies in judge quotas may directly recommend candidates to be appointed to the quota from among the alternate candidates, and after reporting to the High People's Court for approval in accordance with procedures, handle the appointment procedures. Candidates who fail to be appointed as alternates shall participate in the next selection of quota judges in accordance with the same procedures and standards as other persons.

15. As required by work, the High People's Court may adopt methods such as secondment and transfer to adjust and allocate judges together with their used quotas and staffing to courts that need to supplement judges.

16. The High People's Court shall, in light of actual work, study and formulate specific measures for dynamic adjustment and management of judge quotas in its region in accordance with these Opinions.

17. These Opinions shall be interpreted by the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court, and shall come into force as of February 1, 2020.
